description: Self-hostable web-based control plane for running long-running, multi-session coding agents on a project, with a DAG-aware kanban board as the primary interface. v0.1 is the first public release: monorepo with browser frontend (React + Vite + Tailwind), Node.js backend (Fastify + WS), and Python daemon (asyncio + LangGraph); loopback-only single-user single-project; one of four LLM providers (anthropic/openai/bedrock/ollama) selected by the user; persistent bottom dialog drives intent classification and auto-decomposition; drag-to-start execution model; manual mode only (no auto-mode toggle).

features.description: Monorepo skeleton with pnpm workspaces for JS packages and a single Python package; root pyproject.toml + pnpm-workspace.yaml; packages/{web,daemon,cli} directories with package.json or pyproject.toml each
steps: Create pnpm-workspace.yaml at repo root listing packages/*
Create root pyproject.toml that includes the daemon package via pip workspace
Create packages/web/package.json (React+Vite+TypeScript scaffold; no implementation yet)
Create packages/daemon/pyproject.toml (Python 3.11+, asyncio, langgraph, langchain-core)
Create packages/cli/pyproject.toml (click/typer console-script entry point)
Run `pnpm install` and `pip install -e .` from repo root, both succeed with zero errors
Run `pnpm --filter web dev` and verify Vite dev server starts on 5173

features.description: Apache 2.0 LICENSE file at repo root + SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 header in every packages/* source file (.py, .ts, .tsx); license confirmation in README. HARNESS/ keeps its own MIT license (vendored from Anthropic's open-source harness; see HARNESS/README.md).
steps: Place LICENSE file (Apache 2.0 full text) at repo root
Add SPDX header to every Python file under packages/{cli,daemon}/*
Add SPDX header to every TypeScript file under packages/web/*
Add a License section to README.md pointing at LICENSE
Add a notice that HARNESS/ is separately MIT-licensed
Run a script that asserts every .py/.ts/.tsx under packages/* contains the SPDX header; script exits 0

features.description: Structured JSON logging infrastructure shared between Node.js and Python: one line per event to stderr with ts/level/component/project_id/feature_id/event/msg; output filter strips api_key/secret/token from any field name
steps: Create packages/common/heddle_common/logging.py: JSON-line emitter with the documented schema; one event per write to stderr
Implement packages/web/src/lib/logger.ts: equivalent JSON-line emitter for Node.js
Add a filter step in both that strips any field whose name matches api_key/secret/token (case-insensitive, underscore-insensitive)
Unit test: emit a sample event with {api_key: 'xxx'} in payload; assert the serialized line does not contain 'xxx'
Unit test: emit 100 events in rapid succession; assert each is on its own line and parseable as JSON

features.description: GitHub Actions CI workflow at .github/workflows/ci.yml: triggers on PR and push to main; runs install/build/unit/integration under HEDDLE_FAKE_LLM=1; live-LLM E2E tests run on nightly schedule behind a repo secret
steps: Create .github/workflows/ci.yml with on: pull_request and on: push to main
Configure job matrix on ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest
Each job: checkout → setup-node 20 → setup-python 3.11 → pnpm install → pip install -e . → pnpm --filter web build → pnpm test → pytest
All test commands run with HEDDLE_FAKE_LLM=1 in env
Separate workflow at .github/workflows/nightly.yml with cron schedule, gated on LIVE_LLM_TESTS secret, calls the same test commands without HEDDLE_FAKE_LLM
Configure pnpm cache (lockfile-keyed) and pip cache in both workflows

features.description: HEDDLE_FAKE_LLM test fixture: when env var is set, all LLM calls in the daemon return scripted responses from a test fixture file instead of calling real providers; enables CI without API keys or network
steps: Define fixture file format: JSON-lines mapping tool-call sequences to scripted LLM responses
Implement fixtures/ directory under packages/daemon/tests/ with a sample fixture covering a 3-step agent run
Implement fixture loader that reads the file once at daemon startup under HEDDLE_FAKE_LLM=1
Modify the agent runtime to short-circuit real LLM calls and emit the scripted responses when HEDDLE_FAKE_LLM=1
Integration test: run a sample feature end-to-end with HEDDLE_FAKE_LLM=1 and assert it reaches the expected terminal state

features.description: feature_list_io library extraction: shared Python module that wraps HARNESS/tools/feature_list.py mutation logic; both the CLI script and the daemon use this library so there is one source of truth for feature_list.json I/O
steps: Create heddle_common/feature_list_io.py: load(), save(), add(), mark_in_progress(), mark_passing(), mark_blocked(), mark_deferred(), update_metadata() + constants
Refactor HARNESS/tools/_feature_io.py and _feature_state.py to re-export from heddle_common (thin shims)
Refactor HARNESS/tools/feature_list.py to dispatch mutation commands via heddle_common
Run HARNESS/tools/feature_list.py status before and after the refactor; output is byte-identical
Run handoff_check.py before and after; output shows zero new warnings/errors
Run a round-trip test: load() then save() the same JSON; bytes are identical

features.description: schema_version field in feature_list.json root: integer, initial value 1; loaded with default 0 if absent; written always with current version; new daemon refuses files with schema_version > current_max with clear error
steps: Add schema_version: int field to feature_list_io.load() result and to save() output
Add a SCHEMA_VERSION constant (= 1) in heddle_common/
Add SCHEMA_VERSION_MAX = current_max constant (initially equal to SCHEMA_VERSION); bump on every breaking schema change
In load(): if schema_version > SCHEMA_VERSION_MAX, raise SchemaVersionError with message including both versions and instructions to upgrade
Update HARNESS/tools/feature_list.py to preserve schema_version on every read+write cycle
Test: load an old file without schema_version; assert loaded dict has schema_version=0 internally and 1 on disk after save
Test: load a file with schema_version=999; assert SchemaVersionError is raised with clear message

features.description: Add kind/fixes/enhances/superseded_by/implementation_model optional fields to feature objects in feature_list.json; defaults kind=feature, all others null; new daemon recognizes them; old daemon ignores unknown fields without crashing
steps: Add the five optional fields to the feature dict schema in feature_list_io
Defaults: kind=feature, fixes=null, enhances=null, superseded_by=null, implementation_model=null
save() always writes all five fields (even when null) so the on-disk schema is always complete
Validation in add() / update paths: if kind=bugfix then fixes is required and target must exist; if kind=enhancement then enhances is required and target must exist
Test: round-trip a feature with kind=bugfix, fixes=feat-001; both reads return the values
Test: old-format JSON without kind loads with kind defaulting to feature; new-format JSON loads with all fields preserved
Test: save() then load() yields byte-identical JSON (modulo schema_version)

features.description: ~/.heddle/configs.yaml file with pre-populated four LLM provider templates (anthropic-claude-sonnet, openai-gpt-4, bedrock-claude, ollama-llama); on first run, heddle creates the file with these defaults; user picks one, sets env var, ready
steps: Define configs.yaml schema: list of named configs each with provider/model/base_url/api_key_env/api_key (api_key left blank)
Implement first-run UX: if ~/.heddle/configs.yaml does not exist, write the four default templates
Implement parser that loads configs.yaml into a dict keyed by name
Implement writer that updates a single config entry by name
CLI command `heddle configs list` prints the four templates with their filled values
Test: delete ~/.heddle/configs.yaml; run heddle; assert the file is recreated with the four defaults

features.description: ~/.heddle/projects.json registry: list of registered projects with id/name/path/added_at/last_accessed_at; v0.1 supports one project at a time (multi-project concurrent execution is post-v0.1)
steps: Define projects.json schema with the documented fields
Implement loader/writer in heddle_common/
Implement add_project(path) that: validates path exists, computes id (uuid4), records added_at=now
Implement remove_project(id) that: stops execution (post-feat-014 daemon), deletes the project entry, cascades to log files (feat-015)
Test: add a project pointing at a real directory; assert projects.json has the entry
Test: remove a project; assert projects.json no longer has the entry and the log files are gone

features.description: ~/.heddle/.env fallback loader: heddle reads this file on startup and loads KEY=VALUE lines into the process environment; process env vars win; file is gitignored; loose permissions trigger a warning and refuse to start
steps: Implement .env parser: read KEY=VALUE lines, ignore # comments, handle quoted values
On startup, after process env is established, parse ~/.heddle/.env and merge into os.environ (process env takes precedence)
Check file permissions: if mode has any group/other read bit set, log warning and exit with code 1
Generate ~/.heddle/.gitignore on first run that ignores .env
Heddle never writes to ~/.heddle/.env (asserted by a comment in the loader module)
Test: create .env with TEST_VAR=test_value; start a subprocess that reads TEST_VAR; assert the value is test_value
Test: chmod 644 on .env; assert heddle exits with warning and non-zero code

features.description: Project removal cascade: when remove_project(id) is called, the Node.js layer deletes ~/.heddle/logs/<project_id>.log and ~/.heddle/logs/<project_id>/ directory; no retain option in v0.1
steps: Wire feat-012 remove_project() to also delete the per-project log directory
Before deletion, ensure the daemon is no longer writing to those files (stop any in-flight features for that project)
Test: register a project, run a fake log write to its log file, remove the project, assert the log file is gone
Test: remove a project with an in_progress feature; assert the feature is aborted and the log files are deleted

features.description: Log file rotation: 50 MB per file with 5 generations retained; configurable via HEDDLE_LOG_MAX_BYTES and HEDDLE_LOG_BACKUP_COUNT env vars; daemon side uses RotatingFileHandler; Node.js side hand-rolled equivalent
steps: Daemon side: configure logging.handlers.RotatingFileHandler with maxBytes=HEDDLE_LOG_MAX_BYTES (default 50MB) and backupCount=HEDDLE_LOG_BACKUP_COUNT (default 5)
Node.js side: implement ~30 lines that watches file size and renames file to .1, .2, etc. on rotation
Test: write 100 MB of logs to a single project; assert the file rolls over and the oldest generation is deleted
Test: set HEDDLE_LOG_MAX_BYTES=1048576; write 5 MB; assert 5 backup files exist

features.description: Backward-compat tests for feature_list_io: ensure HARNESS-format JSON (without schema_version, kind, fixes, enhances, superseded_by, implementation_model) loads cleanly and saves with the new schema
steps: Create tests/fixtures/old-harness-format.json with a feature_list.json from before any v0.1 changes
Test: load it via feature_list_io; assert all features are readable with kind defaulting to feature
Test: save it back; assert the saved file has schema_version=1 and all new optional fields written
Test: feed it through the HARNESS tools/feature_list.py status command; assert it reports correct metadata counts

features.description: Python daemon skeleton: asyncio process with a websockets server bound to loopback; exposes a single /ws endpoint that accepts JSON-envelope messages; emits structured JSON logs to stderr; hard-fails on port conflict
steps: Create packages/daemon/heddle/daemon/server.py with an asyncio entry point that starts a websockets server on HEDDLE_DAEMON_PORT (default 8765) bound to 127.0.0.1
Implement the JSON envelope parser/serializer (T-010): every message is {v: 1, type: ..., ...}
On startup, attempt to bind the port; if OSError EADDRINUSE, log a clear error message and exit with code 1
On startup, refuse to bind any non-loopback address with a clear error and exit code 1
Test: start daemon; connect a websocket client from 127.0.0.1; assert handshake succeeds
Test: start daemon on port 8765 twice; second instance exits with port-conflict error

features.description: LangGraph checkpointer with SQLite: per-project .heddle/checkpoints.db file in the user's selected project directory; LangGraph threads auto-persist; restoring a thread resumes from the last checkpoint
steps: Configure LangGraph SqliteSaver with checkpoint_db path = <project_path>/.heddle/checkpoints.db
On daemon startup for a project, ensure .heddle/ exists; create checkpoints.db if not present
Implement thread lifecycle: each feature_id maps to one LangGraph thread_id; on resume, the thread loads its last checkpoint and continues
Test: start a feature, interrupt it at step 3 (kill daemon), restart daemon, resume feature; assert it continues from step 3 not step 1
Test: simulate a daemon crash mid-feature via SIGKILL; restart; assert the feature is still recoverable

features.description: Self-written agent runtime (D-053): an LLM <-> tools loop in heddle/daemon/agent_runtime.py that calls LLM, parses tool calls, executes tools, appends results, loops until LLM signals done; NOT using LangChain's prebuilt agent executor
steps: Create agent_runtime.py with an async run_agent_step(thread_id, message) function

Inside run_agent_step: load thread state from checkpointer, build messages (system + history + new), call LLM, parse response (tool calls or final), execute tool calls via tool-dispatch middleware (feat-022), append results to messages, persist thread state, return
Loop until LLM response signals done (e.g., a stop_reason field) or max_steps reached
On recursion_limit (D-052): raise a structured error with cause=recursion_limit
Test: with HEDDLE_FAKE_LLM=1 and a fixture that has 2 tool calls then done; assert agent_runtime completes after 3 LLM invocations

features.description: Six self-written tools (D-053) implementing the LangChain BaseTool interface: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep; each with name + description + args_schema + _run(); no third-party tool libraries
steps: Create heddle/daemon/tools/read.py: reads a file from the project directory, returns content (truncated at configurable size)
Create write.py: writes content to a file in the project directory
Create edit.py: applies a string-replace edit to a file (matches Claude Code's Edit semantics)
Create bash.py: runs a subprocess command in the project directory with a timeout
Create glob.py: returns matching paths via pathlib glob patterns
Create grep.py: returns matching lines via re patterns, with file filter
All tools: args_schema is a Pydantic model (or stdlib dataclass equivalent)
Test: each tool has a unit test covering happy path and one error path (file not found, etc.)

features.description: Sandbox middleware (D-053): a tool-dispatch layer that runs before every tool call; enforces the sandbox level from .heddle/config.yaml (read-only / edit-with-confirm / full); rejects read-only tool calls with synthetic error result; pauses edit-with-confirm tool calls until user responds in the dialog
steps: Define sandbox_level enum in .heddle/config.yaml (read-only / edit-with-confirm / full)
Implement tool_dispatch middleware that intercepts every tool call before execution
For read-only: reject Write/Edit/Bash with synthetic tool result explaining the sandbox is read-only; allow Read/Glob/Grep through
For edit-with-confirm: emit a WS confirm_request event with the proposed tool call; block until WS confirm_response arrives (with timeout)
For full: pass through without checks
Test: set sandbox_level=read-only; attempt Write; assert it returns sandbox-rejected synthetic result and no file is created

features.description: recursion_limit guardrail (D-052) + daemon-internal LLM retry (D-041): LangGraph recursion_limit set to 200 at daemon startup (configurable via HEDDLE_RECURSION_LIMIT); on GraphRecursionError transition feature to red in_progress sub-state; LLM calls retry with exponential backoff 1s->2s->4s, max 3 attempts
steps: Set LangGraph recursion_limit from HEDDLE_RECURSION_LIMIT env var (default 200) at daemon startup
On GraphRecursionError: surface to caller as a structured failure with cause=recursion_limit
Wrap LLM call in retry decorator with exponential backoff: 1s, 2s, 4s, max 3 attempts
On 3rd failure: surface to caller as a structured failure with cause=llm_retry_exhausted
Test: with HEDDLE_FAKE_LLM=1 and a fixture that loops forever; assert recursion_limit triggers at 200 steps and surfaces a structured failure
Test: with a mock LLM that fails twice then succeeds; assert 3 calls happened with correct delays

features.description: Four LLM provider integrations via LangChain: anthropic (claude-sonnet-4-5), openai (gpt-4.x), bedrock (claude-on-bedrock), ollama (local llama3); resolved by configs.yaml named config; uses LangChain chat-model integrations, not prebuilt agent executor
steps: Implement LLM factory in heddle/daemon/llm.py that takes a named config and returns a LangChain BaseChatModel instance

Four branches: provider=anthropic returns ChatAnthropic(model=...), provider=openai returns ChatOpenAI(model=...), provider=bedrock returns ChatBedrock(model=...), provider=ollama returns ChatOllama(model=...)
API key resolution per T-015/T-030: read api_key_env from config, look up in process env (with .env fallback)
On missing key: raise a structured error that the daemon surfaces to the user via WS event
Test: instantiate each of the four providers with a mocked env var; assert the right ChatModel subclass is returned

features.description: Per-feature restart budget (D-051): 3 silent recoveries within any 10-minute sliding window; on budget exhaustion or checkpoint loss, feature transitions to blocked; counter persisted in feature_list.json attempts[]
steps: On daemon crash recovery (post-feat-029 supervisor detects drop, respawns): increment restart counter for the affected feature, persist to attempts[]
Implement sliding window check: if 3 restarts within 10 minutes for the same feature, transition that feature to blocked
Implement checkpoint-loss detection: if checkpoints.db is missing/corrupt for a feature, transition to blocked
Test: simulate 3 daemon restarts within 10 minutes; assert the feature transitions to blocked with clear reason
Test: simulate 2 restarts in 10 minutes, then a 3rd after 11 minutes; assert the 3rd does NOT transition to blocked (window has cleared)

features.description: Daemon-side logging with rotation: structured JSON lines to stderr per T-017; per-project log files at ~/.heddle/logs/<project_id>.log; LLM-call audit log at ~/.heddle/logs/<project_id>/llm-audit.jsonl
steps: Implement JSON-line emitter per feat-005 in the daemon
On daemon startup for a project, ensure ~/.heddle/logs/<project_id>/ exists
Every agent_step invocation appends a line to llm-audit.jsonl with {feature_id, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, latency_ms, outcome}
All log lines use feat-015 rotation
Test: run a fake agent step; assert a line was written to llm-audit.jsonl with the right shape

features.description: Fastify skeleton with @fastify/websocket, @sinclair/typebox for schema validation, and TypeScript strict mode; bound to loopback only; serves HTTP REST API at /api/*; WebSocket at /ws
steps: Create packages/cli/src/server.ts with Fastify instance configured for strict TypeScript
Register @fastify/websocket, @fastify/static, @sinclair/typebox type providers
Bind to 127.0.0.1 only; refuse non-loopback binding with a clear error and exit code 1
Define /api/projects, /api/features, /api/dialog route skeletons returning 501 Not Implemented
Test: start the server; curl http://127.0.0.1:5173/api/projects returns 501
Test: attempt to bind to 0.0.0.0; assert exit with clear error message

features.description: Process supervision (T-011): Node.js spawns the Python daemon as a child process via child_process.spawn; on daemon WS disconnect, waits HEDDLE_DAEMON_RESTART_DELAY_MS (default 500ms) then re-spawns; WS health check is 5-second ping; 3 missed pings trigger respawn
steps: Implement heddle/cli/src/supervisor.ts that spawns the daemon subprocess with stdio inherited and args from env vars
On WS disconnect from daemon: log structured event, wait 500ms, re-spawn
Implement WS ping/pong: every 5 seconds Node.js sends ping; daemon responds with pong; if 3 pings miss, kill daemon and respawn
On daemon process exit (clean or crash): log structured event with exit code
Test: start supervisor with a fake daemon that exits cleanly; assert supervisor respawns after delay
Test: simulate WS disconnect (kill daemon's WS server); assert supervisor respawns

features.description: HTTP REST routes for projects (list/add/remove), features (list/get/transition), dialog (submit message); all with TypeBox schema validation; responses are JSON envelopes
steps: GET /api/projects returns list of registered projects from projects.json
POST /api/projects accepts {path: string} and adds the project (validates path exists)
DELETE /api/projects/:id removes the project (cascades per feat-014)
GET /api/projects/:id/features returns feature list with status/depends_on/etc
POST /api/projects/:id/features/:fid/transition accepts {action: retry|abandon|mark-done}
POST /api/projects/:id/dialog accepts {message: string}; returns the dialog response (intent classification + draft cards or chat response)
All routes validate input via TypeBox schemas; invalid input returns 400 with validation errors
Test: each route has a Vitest test covering happy path and one validation failure

features.description: Browser<->Node.js WebSocket event stream: client connects to /ws on the Node.js backend; server pushes project_id-tagged events (feature.status_changed, feature.attempt_started, feature.attempt_finished, etc.); client sends dialog messages and commands
steps: Implement WS handler at /ws in the Fastify server using @fastify/websocket
Define event types: feature.status_changed, feature.attempt_started, feature.attempt_finished, feature.diagnosis, dag.topology_changed, daemon.health, daemon.crashed, project.dialog_response
Each event has {v: 1, type, project_id, payload}
Server-side: maintain a registry of connected clients; on daemon events from feat-030, broadcast to clients filtered by project_id
Test: simulate a feature status change; assert all connected clients receive the event within 100ms
Test: two clients connected, two projects; event for project A only reaches the client viewing project A

features.description: Node.js <-> Daemon WebSocket protocol handler: Node.js connects to daemon WS at ws://127.0.0.1:8765; bidirectional message flow with JSON envelopes; commands (start_feature, stop_feature, retry_feature, dialog_turn) and events (feature_progress, feature_done, feature_failed, log_line)
steps: Implement heddle/cli/src/daemon-client.ts that opens WS to the daemon at startup
Define command types sent Node.js -> daemon: start_feature, stop_feature, retry_feature, dialog_turn
Define event types sent daemon -> Node.js: feature_progress, feature_done, feature_failed, log_line, diagnosis
Forward daemon events to the Browser<->Node.js WS layer per feat-029
Test: send start_feature command; assert daemon begins execution and emits feature_progress events
Test: send stop_feature; assert daemon halts and emits feature_done with outcome=stopped

features.description: LLM config resolution: when a feature is started, Node.js passes the feature's implementation_model (locked config name) to the daemon; daemon looks up the config in ~/.heddle/configs.yaml and instantiates the LLM via feat-023 factory
steps: Step 1: Add resolve_feature_llm_config(name_or_none, configs_path) in packages/daemon/heddle_daemon/llm_config.py; on None return first list_configs() entry with source="default"; on string call get_config and return source="explicit"; on missing/unknown raise LLMConfigError with cause="llm_config_error"

Step 2: Add build_llm_for_feature(cfg, *, fixture_root, env) in agent_runtime.py wrapping fake_llm_or_real(real_factory=lambda: build_chat_model(cfg, env=env), fixture_path=fixture_root/<feature_id>.json if fixture_root else None, env=env); export from __all__

Step 3: Extend DaemonConfig with configs_path (default ~/.heddle/configs.yaml) and fixture_root (default ~/.heddle/fake_fixtures); honor HEDDLE_CONFIGS_PATH and HEDDLE_FAKE_LLM_FIXTURE_ROOT in run_daemon; thread through enable_routes() into RouteHandler

Step 4: In RouteHandler, _start_feature and _retry_feature read the feature row, resolve implementation_model via llm_config.resolve_feature_llm_config, build the LLM via build_llm_for_feature, register it on RouteHandler._attempt_llms keyed by attempt_id, emit llm_resolved event (payload {attempt_id, config_name, source}) between feature_attempt_started and the terminal response; on LLMConfigError return ok=false error.code="llm_config_error" and emit no llm_resolved event
Step 5: Node.js protocol.ts: add implementation_model?: string|null to BrowserCommandEnvelope; parseBrowserCommand strips the field for start_feature / retry_feature only

Step 6: Node.js routes/features.ts: add POST /api/projects/:id/features/:fid/start and POST .../retry endpoints forwarding implementation_model to the daemon via forwardOrFail; StartOrRetryBodySchema TypeBox

Step 7: Tests: test_llm_config.py (explicit hit, null default, unknown name, missing file, fake-LLM short-circuit); test_routes_start_feature.py (WS round-trip with explicit/null/unknown); extend test_commands_protocol.py to assert both feature_attempt_started AND llm_resolved events emitted in order
Step 8: Validation: handoff_check, ruff check, ruff format --check, pnpm --filter node typecheck, pytest packages/common/heddle_common/tests + packages/daemon/tests -v
Step 9: Mark feat-031 passing via feature_list.py mark-passing only after Steps 1-8 green end-to-end

features.description: Vite + React + Tailwind v4 + TypeScript (strict mode) skeleton in packages/web; Zustand for UI state, TanStack Query for server state; one-page app (no router) with project switcher
steps: Scaffold Vite project with React-TS template
Install Tailwind v4 + @tailwindcss/vite plugin; configure
Install zustand and @tanstack/react-query
Set up TypeScript strict mode (strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes)
App.tsx renders a single <App /> with a project switcher and a placeholder for the kanban + dialog
Run `pnpm --filter web dev`; assert browser loads at http://localhost:5173

features.description: WebSocket client with reconnect wrapper (T-027): native WebSocket API + ~30 lines of glue for state machine (connecting/open/reconnecting/closed), exponential backoff reconnect (1s->2s->4s->8s, cap 30s), event buffering during disconnect (cap 1000 events or 30s)
steps: Implement packages/web/src/lib/ws-client.ts wrapping native WebSocket
Expose connect(), send(message), on(event, handler), close()
On disconnect: exponential backoff reconnect with cap
Buffer outgoing messages while disconnected (cap 1000 events or 30s, then drop oldest)
Emit state change events so UI can show connection status
Test: start server, connect client, kill server, restart server; assert client reconnects automatically and queued messages are sent

features.description: Project switcher UI: dropdown in the header showing all registered projects; click switches the active project; on first run with no projects, show a folder picker to add the first project
steps: Header component shows current project name + a dropdown of all projects
Clicking a project name in the dropdown calls /api/projects/:id/select (or equivalent) and reloads the kanban with that project's features
On first run with zero projects, render an empty state with a 'Pick a project folder' button
Clicking 'Pick a folder' invokes a native folder picker (Tauri/Electron-style dialog); on selection, POST /api/projects
Test: with two projects registered, switch between them; assert the kanban renders the correct features
Test: with zero projects, the empty state shows; clicking add-project triggers the folder picker

features.description: Kanban board with @dnd-kit/core (T-007): three columns (in_progress / ready / blocked), responsive layout, drag-and-drop between columns with single-active model enforcement
steps: Install @dnd-kit/core and @dnd-kit/sortable
Render the kanban with three columns side-by-side (in_progress / ready / blocked)
Each column lists feature cards sortable by drag
Drag a card from ready to in_progress: optimistically update UI, send POST /api/projects/:id/features/:fid/transition
Single-active model: if a card is already in in_progress, the new drag is rejected with a clear error toast
Drag a card from blocked to ready: rejected (blocked features are locked per D-016)
Test: drag a ready card to in_progress; assert the kanban shows it there and the API call succeeded

features.description: Bottom-lane rendering (D-056): Done / Someday / Archive collapsible lanes below the main columns; Done default-expanded; Someday and Archive default-collapsed; lane headers always show counts
steps: Render three collapsible lanes below the kanban main columns: Done (passing), Someday (deferred), Archive (superseded_by != null)
Done is default-expanded; Someday and Archive are default-collapsed
Lane headers always show counts (e.g., '▶ Someday (3)')
Hovering a collapsed-lane count previews the top 3 titles in a tooltip
Lane interactions are view-only: no drag in or out of lanes; no inline edit; modifications go through dialog commands
Test: render a project with 5 passing + 3 deferred + 2 superseded features; assert lane counts and default expansion states

features.description: Card rendering with kind icon (D-024): bugfix cards get an orange left-edge stripe + wrench icon; feature cards get default styling; status-aware badges (in_progress / passing / blocked / deferred)
steps: Card component renders title + description preview + status badge + kind icon (if bugfix)
Bugfix cards: orange left-edge stripe + wrench icon in top-right corner
Blocked cards: lock icon + the blocking dependency (@feat-XXX)
Deferred cards: clock icon + deferred_until date
Passing cards: checkmark + completion timestamp
Test: render cards of each kind and status; assert correct visual treatment per the design

features.description: Persistent bottom dialog (D-014): always visible at the bottom of the board; user types natural-language commands or feature requests; sends to /api/dialog; displays streaming response
steps: Render a textarea + send button at the bottom of the kanban, fixed position
On submit: POST /api/projects/:id/dialog with the user's message
Display the response (text or draft cards or chat reply) inline below the textarea
On chat reply (no cards generated): just show the text response
On draft cards: show a draft tray above the kanban with the cards (feat-040)
Test: type a feature request; assert the dialog response appears; click 'Confirm all' and assert cards become features

features.description: @feat-XXX mention syntax with autocomplete dropdown (D-034): typing @ in the dialog opens a list of matching features by id / title / description; arrow keys to navigate, Enter to insert
steps: When user types @ in the dialog textarea, show a popup with matching features
Filter as user types more characters (matched against id + title + description)
Show 6 candidates at a time with scrolling
Arrow keys to navigate, Enter to confirm (inserts '@feat-XXX '), Esc to dismiss
Test: type @fe in dialog; assert dropdown shows feat-001, feat-002 etc.; press Enter on feat-003; assert textarea now has '@feat-003 '

features.description: Draft cards UI (D-013/D-044/D-045): draft tray appears above the kanban when dialog returns cards; cards have temp-XXX ids; user can keep/uncheck them; clicking 'Confirm all (N)' inserts them as feat-XXX
steps: Draft tray renders above the kanban when /api/dialog returns draft cards
Each draft card shows title + description + checkbox (default unchecked = may be removed by next decomposition)
User types more in dialog: re-decomposition runs, drafts are rewritten (kept cards are preserved verbatim, others may change/disappear)
Click 'Confirm all (N)' button at the bottom of the tray; calls /api/confirm-drafts with the kept card ids; on success, tray clears
Test: type 'add OAuth login'; assert draft tray shows 1-3 cards; click 'Confirm all'; assert the kanban now has the new feature

features.description: DAG view with reactflow (D-058): right-side slide-in panel with bidirectional sync to kanban; ego-network highlight on node click; pan/zoom + fit-to-screen; fullscreen on narrow viewports
steps: Install @xyflow/react (reactflow v12)
Render DAG nodes (one per feature) and edges (depends_on) with status-based colors
Open DAG view: panel slides in from the right; kanban compresses to make room
Divider between kanban and DAG is draggable to resize
Click a kanban card: select matching DAG node, highlight ego-network (node + parents + children + edges), dim everything else
Click a DAG node: select matching kanban card, scroll to make it visible, apply ego-network highlight
On viewport < 1280px: DAG view promotes to fullscreen overlay (no side panel)
Test: open DAG view; click a blocked feature; assert its ancestors + descendants are highlighted

features.description: Diagnosis structured report UI (D-035): when user invokes @feat-XXX diagnose, the LLM produces {cause, suggestion, diff?}; UI renders this as a card with three sections
steps: When user types '@feat-XXX 分析 ...' in dialog, server returns a structured diagnosis
UI renders a diagnosis card with three sections: cause, suggestion, diff (if present)
If diff is present, show before/after side by side with an 'Apply' button
Apply button triggers retry-with-hint per feat-043
Test: invoke diagnose on a failed feature; assert the card renders all three sections

features.description: Failure handling dialog commands (D-033): diagnose / retry / retry-with-hint / mark-done / abandon; each @feat-XXX + natural-language command invokes the corresponding handler
steps: Parse dialog input for @feat-XXX patterns + command verbs (diagnose / retry / retry-with-hint / mark-done / abandon)
On retry-with-hint: server returns a proposed diff before re-running; UI shows the diff and a 'Confirm' button; on confirm, server re-runs the feature with the hint
On abandon: server marks the feature as deferred/superseded; UI confirms with the user first
On mark-done: server transitions the feature to passing (with a warning that no actual work was done)
Test: type '@feat-003 retry'; assert the feature transitions back to ready and a new run begins

features.description: Intent classification (D-017): the daemon classifies user dialog input as 'chat' (no cards generated, plain response) or 'work' (cards generated); chat responses are streamed back without entering draft flow
steps: Implement classify_intent() in the daemon that takes user input and returns 'chat' or 'work'
For chat: respond with a plain text message (no draft cards)
For work: enter the decomposition flow (feat-045)
The classification prompt is part of the dialog_model's system prompt
Test: send a chat message ('hi how are you'); assert response is plain text with no draft cards
Test: send a work message ('add OAuth login'); assert response has draft cards

features.description: Auto-decomposition (D-002/D-006/D-008/D-029): when work intent is detected, the LLM proposes one or more draft features with id (temp-XXX), title, description, steps, depends_on; full feature_list is in the prompt for context
steps: Implement decompose(user_input, feature_list) in the daemon that returns list of draft feature dicts

System prompt includes: target granularity (30-80 agent steps), DAG constraints (depends_on must exist), classification heuristic (loose similarity = no surface; partial = suggest enhancement; strong duplicate = 3-way clarification)
Draft cards have id=tmp-XXX (auto-generated), title, description, steps (3-7), depends_on, optional kind/fixes
Pass the full feature_list (id + title + description of each) to the LLM as context per D-029
Test: send 'add OAuth login' with an empty feature list; assert 1-2 draft cards returned with realistic steps

features.description: DAG satisfiability validation (D-003/D-004/D-027): at confirm time, validate that all draft cards' depends_on references existing features; reject drafts with non-existent deps; algorithm decides feature status (pending/blocked) from DAG topology
steps: Implement validate_drafts(drafts, feature_list) that checks every depends_on exists
On invalid: return clear error message, do not insert
On valid: for each new feature, compute initial status from DAG topology: status=pending if all deps=passing, else status=blocked
Test: submit drafts with depends_on referring to a non-existent feat-XXX; assert validation rejects

features.description: Crash recovery via checkpoint resume (D-051): when daemon restarts mid-feature, in-flight threads are restored from SQLite checkpoints; user is unaware; restart budget per feature limits silent recovery
steps: On daemon startup, list active threads (those with checkpoints but not terminal state)
For each active thread: resume execution from the latest checkpoint
On resume, increment the feature's restart counter; check budget per feat-024
Test: start a feature with HEDDLE_FAKE_LLM=1; kill the daemon at step 5 of 10; restart daemon; assert the feature resumes at step 5 and completes

features.description: Structured event log: every state-changing operation (status transition, attempt start/finish, draft confirm, dialog submit) emits a structured event to the WS stream and to per-project logs
steps: Define event types per feat-029
At each state-change site (feature_list_io mark_*, dialog handlers, daemon lifecycle), emit a structured event
Events flow: daemon -> Node.js -> Browser WS + per-project log file
Test: trigger a feature transition; assert the WS event reaches the browser and the log file has a matching line

features.description: End-to-end happy path test: user adds a project, types 'add X' in dialog, confirms draft, drags card to in_progress, agent executes via HEDDLE_FAKE_LLM, feature transitions to passing
steps: Playwright test: open heddle at http://localhost:5173 (test harness starts everything)
Click 'Add project', pick a test fixture directory with a real feature_list.json
Type 'add a hello world feature' in dialog; assert draft card appears
Click 'Confirm all'; assert new feature appears in ready column
Drag the new feature to in_progress; with HEDDLE_FAKE_LLM=1 and a fixture that completes in 2 steps, assert the feature transitions to passing

features.description: `heddle start` command (T-003): launches Node.js backend (which supervises Python daemon); auto-opens browser to http://localhost:5173; refuses non-loopback binding
steps: Implement `heddle start` console-script entry point in packages/cli
It spawns the Node.js server (which in turn supervises the daemon)
On successful startup, opens default browser to http://localhost:5173
On port conflict, clear error and non-zero exit
On non-loopback binding request, clear error and non-zero exit
Test: run heddle start in a temp project; assert browser opens, server is reachable, daemon is alive

features.description: `heddle dev` command (T-019): starts Vite dev server (5173) + Node.js backend (5174) + daemon; Vite proxies /api and /ws to Fastify; hot reload on file changes for all three
steps: Implement `heddle dev` console-script entry point
Spawns three processes: Vite dev server, Node.js backend, Python daemon
Vite config proxies /api and /ws to http://localhost:5174
Node.js backend uses tsx --watch for hot reload of TypeScript code
Daemon uses watchfiles for Python code hot reload
Test: run heddle dev; edit a React component; assert browser hot-reloads; edit a Python tool; assert daemon reloads

features.description: `heddle test` command: runs the full test pyramid - Vitest for JS, pytest for Python, Playwright for browser E2E; all under HEDDLE_FAKE_LLM=1 by default; exits non-zero on any failure
steps: Implement `heddle test` console-script entry point
Runs: pnpm test (Vitest in packages/web + packages/cli) -> pytest (packages/daemon) -> pnpm --filter web test:e2e (Playwright)
HEDDLE_FAKE_LLM=1 in env for deterministic test responses
Aggregates exit codes; exits 0 only if all pass
Test: run heddle test in a clean checkout; assert exits 0
Test: deliberately break a test; assert exits non-zero

features.description: `heddle lint` command: runs ESLint on JS/TS, Ruff on Python, TypeScript --noEmit on TS; reports all issues; exits non-zero on any error
steps: Implement `heddle lint` console-script entry point
Runs: eslint . (across packages), ruff check . (across Python), tsc --noEmit (across TS projects)
Aggregates exit codes; exits 0 only if all pass
Test: run heddle lint in a clean checkout; assert exits 0

features.description: Post-confirm feature modification (D-054): split / merge / edit / reprioritize / add-dep / remove-dep via natural-language dialog commands referencing @feat-XXX; destructive ops show diff before execution; superseded features hide from main view
steps: Implement parse_modify_command(dialog_input, feature_list) that returns the requested operation
On split: produce new draft cards + mark original with superseded_by; downstream features get new depends_on
On merge: combine features into one; originals marked superseded_by
On edit: show diff of proposed change; user confirms before applying
On reprioritize / add-dep / remove-dep: apply directly (non-destructive)
Test: type '@feat-003 拆成 3 个'; assert 3 draft cards produced and feat-003 marked superseded

features.description: Sandbox enforcement in Web UI (D-053): the per-project sandbox level (read-only / edit-with-confirm / full) is set in .heddle/config.yaml; UI shows the current level; on edit-with-confirm, shows a confirm dialog before destructive tool calls
steps: Settings panel in the project switcher shows current sandbox_level
User can change it (writes to .heddle/config.yaml)
On edit-with-confirm + agent tool call requiring confirmation: WS event triggers a modal in the browser
User clicks 'Approve' or 'Deny' in the modal; response goes back to the daemon via WS
Test: set sandbox=edit-with-confirm; trigger a Write tool call; assert the browser shows a confirm modal

features.description: Kanban filter dropdown (D-024): in the kanban header, a dropdown lets user filter by kind (all / features / bugfixes / enhancements); filter applies to all three columns + lanes
steps: Add a filter dropdown in the kanban header with options: all / features / bugfixes / enhancements
Filter state lives in Zustand
Filtered-out cards are hidden from all columns + lanes
Filter persists in localStorage so it survives page reload
Test: with bugfix + feature cards, switch filter to bugfixes; assert only bugfix cards are visible
